title: When the teeth are gone
odia:
ଆଖୁ, କାକୁଡ଼ି, ନଡ଼ିଆ , ମକା
ଦାନ୍ତ ପଡ଼ିଲେ ତଳକୁ ପକା।
literal_meaning: Sugarcane, cucumber, coconut, maize—when your teeth fall out, put them down.
meaning_odia: ଦାନ୍ତ ନଥିଲେ ଆଗରୁ ଚୋବାଇ ଖାଉଥିବା ଜିନିଷକୁ ଛାଡ଼ିବାକୁ ପଡ଼େ—ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରରେ ସାମର୍ଥ୍ୟ ବଦଳିଲେ ଅଭ୍ୟାସ ବଦଳାଇବାର କଥାକୁ ଏଠାରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି।
explanation: The four foods lead into a blunt instruction: once the teeth are gone, put the food down. This edition reads the scene as a reminder that changed abilities can require changed habits. The warning stays concrete, with the mouth’s ability to chew setting the limit.
usage_example: In a story about growing older, a character recalls these lines while admitting that an old habit has become difficult. This is a newly composed reading example, not recorded traditional usage.
cultural_context: The rhyme of ମକା and ପକା links the food list to its closing instruction. The verse does not discuss how foods are prepared or adapted. It is recorded here as a proverbial image of changed capacity, not dietary or dental advice.
